md_description: This workflow models a clinical registry for prostate cancer patients receiving radiotherapy, starting from the patient cohort and source clinical records, then capturing demographics, comorbidities, treatment plans, session attendance, adverse reactions, and follow-up outcomes. The raw registry extracts are harmonized into an analysis-ready dataset that supports evaluation of radiotherapy protocol effects on survival and quality-of-life outcomes.

prostate_cancer_patient_cohort.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic cohort-level identifiers and properties that define who is in the registry: cohort identity, disease/population scope, treatment context, enrollment timing, and cohort size. I excluded any fields about captured demographics, treatment plans, session events, outcomes, file artifacts, or analysis outputs because those belong to downstream Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any identifier fields that would typically be generated at the root only if already present elsewhere in the DAG; since no prior generated fields were provided, I limited the schema to non-overlapping cohort descriptors rather than patient-level variables.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for this enrolled cohort in the registry, used to reference the patient population record; format example: PCCOHORT_001.
Primary cancer site defining the cohort at enrollment; this registry is focused on prostate cancer patients.
Clinical treatment context required for membership in this cohort; patients are enrolled if they are receiving radiotherapy for prostate cancer.
High-level basis used to include patients in this cohort, describing the population definition rather than an analytic variable; measured at cohort assembly from source records.
Date when the first eligible patient was enrolled into this cohort in the registry; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
Date when cohort enrollment closed or the current extraction ended; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
Total number of patients included in this cohort at the time of registry extraction; integer count of unique enrolled patients.
How long and under what general registry logic the cohort is followed after radiotherapy initiation; describes cohort-level follow-up structure, not individual outcomes.

clinical_source_records.reasoning: This is an Entity node representing the source record corpus itself, so I included fields that describe the provenance, scope, and identity of the underlying clinical records, not the patient demographics, treatment plans, events, or outcomes contained within them. I avoided duplicating downstream Capture/Signal territory such as abstraction settings, file formats, extract sizes, or harmonization details. Since no already_generated fields were provided for this turn, I still kept the schema focused on record-level characteristics like record system, record type, source institution, and date coverage, which help users understand and trace the origin of the registry inputs.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for the source-record collection used by this workflow; format example: SRCREC_001.
Name of the hospital, oncology, or electronic record system where the source clinical records originate; measured at source inventory time.

Primary type of clinical documentation represented in this source corpus, such as oncology notes, treatment planning records, encounter notes, or follow-up visit records; categorical values should reflect the dominant record class.
Name of the hospital, cancer center, or clinical institution that produced the source records; recorded from the originating institution metadata.
Earliest clinical record date available in this source corpus for the cohort; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
Latest clinical record date available in this source corpus for the cohort; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
Primary language used in the source records, relevant for abstraction and harmonization; categorical value recorded from the document corpus.

How the clinical source records were accessed for registry use, describing the record provenance pathway rather than the extraction method; examples include direct system access or scanned document review.

registry_abstraction_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the abstraction session and instrument/configuration details that describe how the registry abstraction was performed: who/what system carried it out, the abstraction method, coding standards, abstraction window, and quality control. I excluded the actual demographic and comorbidity values because those belong on the downstream Signal node, and I avoided file/storage fields because Capture nodes should not describe output artefacts. No already_generated fields were provided for this turn, so I did not need to suppress overlaps beyond keeping the schema strictly within capture-operation territory.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for the abstraction session or batch used to enter structured registry data; format example: ABS_2024_001.
Primary method used by clinical data abstractors to extract patient demographics and comorbidity information from source records into the registry system; record at the time abstraction is performed.
Name of the registry abstraction software or interface used during capture, if applicable; measured from the capture configuration.
Version of the abstraction software or registry interface used during capture; record the exact release or build string used for the session.
Clinical terminology or coding standard used to normalize structured demographics and comorbidity fields during abstraction; captured as part of the registry configuration.
Date when the abstraction session started for this batch of source records; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
Date when the abstraction session ended for this batch of source records; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
Whether the abstracted registry entry passed internal quality assurance review for completeness and consistency at the capture stage.
Identifier for the clinical data abstractor or abstraction team member responsible for the capture session; format example: ABSR_12.

demographics_raw_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw data artefact properties: what the extract contains, its row/column structure, technical file characteristics, schema version, and basic completeness/consistency metrics. I excluded capture settings, source-record provenance, patient identity fields, and harmonization outputs because those belong to upstream Capture/Entity nodes or downstream Process/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so I focused on signal-level descriptors that would let a downstream user store, validate, and reuse the raw demographics extract without repeating the actual demographic values themselves.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for this raw demographics extract file or table; format example: DEMO_RAW_001.
Technical file format of the raw demographics extract at the point it is written or exported, such as CSV, TSV, or Parquet; record the exact storage format used.
Size of the raw demographics data artefact in bytes at the time of storage or export; useful for integrity checks and reproducibility.
Number of patient-level records contained in the raw demographics extract; measured after the capture step and before harmonization.
Number of fields or columns in the raw demographics extract; measured from the structured signal as stored.
Version label for the raw demographics data schema used in this extract; format example: v1.0 or 2024_06.
Proportion of expected raw demographic/comorbidity fields present in the extract, expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1 or percentage-equivalent decimal; assess at the raw signal validation stage.
Count of duplicate patient-level rows detected in the raw demographics extract before any harmonization or deduplication.

radiotherapy_plan_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the configuration and session details of how radiotherapy planning information was abstracted from planning records: capture method, planning system identity, software version, plan review timing, and QC. I excluded the actual dose, target volume, and fractionation values because those belong on the downstream Signal node, and I avoided output-file properties because Capture nodes should not describe the produced artefact. No already_generated fields were provided for this turn, so I did not need to suppress overlaps beyond staying within capture-operation territory and including the agent/hardware-software properties required for operation nodes.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for the radiotherapy plan capture session or batch; format example: RPCAP_2024_001.
Primary radiotherapy planning record source used during capture, such as treatment planning system or planning chart review; record at the time of abstraction.
Name of the radiotherapy planning software or system used as the operational capture platform, if applicable; recorded from the active configuration.
Version of the radiotherapy planning software or system used for capture; use the exact release string available during the session.
Method used by treatment planning staff or registry abstraction to obtain dose, target volume, and fractionation details from planning records; record during the capture session.
Date when the plan details were reviewed or abstracted into the registry capture workflow; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
General radiotherapy plan class being captured, describing the treatment plan context rather than the numeric plan parameters themselves.
Whether the captured plan details passed the capture-stage consistency check for completeness and plausibility.
Identifier for the planning staff member or registry abstractor responsible for the capture session; format example: OPS_17.

plan_raw_signal.reasoning: I corrected the Signal-node schema to avoid cross-step field-id collisions by renaming the generic technical fields that had already been used elsewhere in the DAG. I kept only raw-treatment-plan artefact descriptors and quality metrics that belong to the plan signal, while preserving the same semantic meaning with plan-specific field names. I did not include capture settings, source properties, or downstream harmonization outputs.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for the raw treatment-plan extract file or table; format example: PLAN_RAW_001.
Technical file format of the raw treatment-plan extract at the point of storage or export, such as DICOM-RT export, CSV, TSV, or JSON; record the exact format used.
Size of the raw treatment-plan artefact in bytes at the time it is written or exported; useful for integrity checks and reproducibility.
Number of distinct treatment plans contained in the raw extract; measured after capture and before harmonization.
Number of data fields or columns present in the raw treatment-plan extract; measured from the stored signal.
Version label for the raw treatment-plan schema used in this extract; format example: v1.0 or 2024_06.
Proportion of expected raw treatment-plan fields that are missing in the extract, expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1; assessed at the raw signal validation stage.
Count of duplicate plan rows or repeated plan entries detected in the raw treatment-plan extract before any harmonization.

treatment_session_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I kept only session-level capture configuration and operational descriptors and removed the colliding field capture_quality_flag. I included identifiers, event-capture mode, adverse-event recording method, coding standard, timing, operator identity, and session source because these describe how treatment-session attendance and acute adverse reactions were recorded. I excluded raw attendance/adverse-event values, downstream signal artifacts, and any field names known to collide across DAG steps such as capture_quality_flag, file_format, file_size_bytes, and schema_version.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for the treatment-session capture batch or session group; format example: TSCAP_2024_001.
Mode used to record whether each radiotherapy session was attended, missed, or delayed; capture this at the time of registry entry.
Method used to record acute adverse reactions during each treatment session, such as clinician note abstraction or direct patient-reported entry; measured during the capture session.
Coding or classification standard used to label attendance events and acute adverse reactions during capture; record the standard active in the registry workflow.
Date when this treatment-session capture batch began; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
Date when this treatment-session capture batch ended; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
Identifier for the registry staff member or team responsible for entering the treatment-session events; format example: OPS_17.
Primary source of the session event information used during capture, such as clinic note, treatment record, or patient report; captured as part of the registry workflow.

session_event_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw event-artefact descriptors for the session-event extract: file identity, event granularity, record counts, technical format, storage size, and raw-quality indicators. I excluded capture settings, operator details, and the scientific content values themselves because attendance and adverse reactions are the payload of the signal and should not be repeated as metadata fields. I also avoided previously colliding generic names such as file_format, file_size_bytes, schema_version, and capture_quality_flag, using distinct session-event-specific names instead.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for the raw session-event extract file or table; format example: SESS_EVT_RAW_001.

Level of detail represented in the raw session-event extract, describing whether records are per treatment session, per attendance event, or per adverse event observation; measured from the stored signal.
Total number of raw event records in the session-event extract at the time of storage or export; counted before harmonization.
Number of distinct treatment sessions represented in the raw session-event extract; measured from the raw signal table.
Technical file format of the raw session-event extract at the point of storage or export; record the exact format used.
Size of the raw session-event data artefact in bytes at the time it is written or exported; useful for integrity checks and reproducibility.
Proportion of expected session-event fields missing in the raw extract, expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1; assessed during raw signal validation.
Count of duplicate attendance or adverse-event records detected in the raw session-event extract before any harmonization.
Whether the raw session-event extract passed basic structural validation at the signal stage, such as parsability and record-count checks.

followup_outcome_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the follow-up session and instrument configuration details: how follow-up was conducted, when it occurred, which outcomes were targeted, what quality-of-life instrument was used, and who/system performed the capture. I excluded the actual survival status, time-to-event values, and QoL scores because those belong on the downstream Signal node, and I avoided file/storage and analysis fields. I also kept away from previously colliding generic names like capture_quality_flag, file_format, file_size_bytes, and schema_version by using follow-up-specific operational names instead.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for the follow-up outcome capture batch or encounter group; format example: FUCAP_2024_001.
Type of follow-up encounter used to capture post-radiotherapy outcome information; record at the time the visit is scheduled or completed.
Outcome domains actively captured during the follow-up encounter, describing the measurement scope rather than the measured values themselves.
Name of the questionnaire or instrument used to collect quality-of-life measurements during follow-up, if applicable; recorded at the follow-up capture session.
Date on which the follow-up outcome capture occurred; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
Elapsed time in months from radiotherapy completion to the follow-up capture point; measured when the encounter is recorded, typically ranging from 0 to multiple years.
Identifier for the registry staff member or clinical system responsible for capturing the follow-up encounter; format example: OPS_17.
Whether the follow-up encounter capture passed initial completeness and consistency checks at the capture stage.
Primary source used to capture the follow-up encounter, such as clinic note, patient-reported questionnaire, or chart abstraction; recorded as part of the capture process.

outcome_raw_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node. I kept only raw follow-up artefact descriptors and renamed overlapping generic technical fields to avoid DAG-wide collisions: instead of record_count and artifact_size_bytes, I used outcome_record_count and outcome_artifact_size_bytes. I excluded capture details and the actual survival/QoL values because they belong to the capture and data-content layers, not the signal metadata. The schema therefore focuses on raw outcome extract identity, content scope, structure, validation, and storage characteristics without duplicating earlier fields.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for the raw follow-up outcome extract file or table; format example: OUT_RAW_001.
Primary follow-up outcome domain represented in the raw extract, describing what the signal contains at a high level; measured from the stored raw data.
Total number of follow-up outcome records in the raw extract at the time of storage or export; counted before harmonization.
Number of unique patients represented in the raw follow-up outcome extract; measured from the raw signal table.
Technical file format of the raw outcome extract at the point of storage or export; record the exact format used.
Size of the raw outcome data artefact in bytes at the time it is written or exported; useful for integrity checks and reproducibility.
Proportion of expected follow-up outcome fields missing in the raw extract, expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1; assessed during raw signal validation.
Count of duplicate follow-up outcome rows detected in the raw extract before any harmonization or deduplication.
Whether the raw follow-up outcome extract passed basic structural and integrity validation at the signal stage.

harmonize_registry_tables.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the harmonization operation itself: cleaning, standardization, linkage logic, key parameters, software/runtime, and output-quality indicators. I excluded upstream raw signal properties, downstream dataset properties, and any patient-level scientific variables because those do not belong to the transformation step. I also avoided repeating already generated fields and the known colliding generic names like record_count and artifact_size_bytes; instead I used process-specific names for linkage completeness, normalization rules, and validation outcomes that describe how the registry tables were harmonized.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for this harmonization execution or batch; format example: HARM_2024_001.
Name of the software or script environment used to harmonize the registry tables; for process nodes this identifies the computing agent, such as a Python pipeline or ETL package.
Version of the harmonization software or pipeline used for cleaning, standardizing, and linking the registry extracts; record the exact release string used in the run.
Code repository or provenance location for the harmonization workflow, if available; use a stable URL or repository identifier.
Primary strategy used to link patient, plan, session, and follow-up tables into a unified registry dataset; record at the time the harmonization step is executed.
Ruleset or reference standard applied to normalize terminology, dates, units, and categorical labels during harmonization; measured as part of the transformation specification.
Method used to resolve duplicate records encountered during merging of the structured extracts; describes the harmonization logic rather than raw duplicate counts.
Proportion of expected cross-table links successfully created during harmonization, expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1; assess after table linkage and before dataset release.
Whether the unified registry dataset passed the harmonization-stage validation checks for consistency, referential integrity, and standardization.

analysis_ready_dataset.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I kept only properties of the computed analysis-ready table itself: dataset identity, analytic granularity, content coverage, linkage/validation status, and release timing. I excluded raw counts that collide with earlier signal metadata such as row_count, column_count, and patient_count, and avoided upstream process details or downstream statistical results. The schema now uses derivative-specific quality and structure fields that describe the output of harmonization without repeating already generated identifiers or generic count names.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for the analysis-ready dataset; format example: ARD_001.
Analytic level of the unified table produced by the harmonization step, describing the unit of observation represented in each row.
Registry domains represented in the final dataset, describing the content scope of the derivative rather than the source signals.

Proportion of expected links across patient, plan, session, and follow-up domains that were successfully retained in the analysis-ready dataset, expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1; assessed after harmonization and before analysis.
Proportion of expected fields missing in the final analysis-ready dataset, expressed as a fraction from 0 to 1; assessed after harmonization and before analysis.
Whether the unified patient-level table passed referential integrity checks across linked registry domains at release time.
Date when the analysis-ready dataset was finalized and released for downstream statistical analysis; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
Version label assigned to the analysis-ready dataset release, allowing downstream users to distinguish successive harmonized builds; format example: v1.0 or 2024_06.

protocol_outcome_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only analysis-operation fields and avoided the already-colliding generic software metadata names software_name, software_version, and repository_url. I kept the schema focused on the statistical model specification, adjustment logic, diagnostics, and timing for the protocol-outcome analysis. I excluded raw dataset properties and downstream effect estimates because those belong to other nodes, and used alternative process-specific names for the computational environment and model assessment.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for this statistical modeling run; format example: ANA_2024_001.

Name of the statistical computing environment or analysis platform used to run the protocol-outcome models; for process nodes this identifies the agent executing the analysis, such as R, Python, or SAS.
Version of the computing environment or analysis platform used for the analysis; record the exact release string used in the run.
Code repository, script archive, or provenance location for the analysis workflow; use a stable URL or repository identifier if available.
Statistical model family used to evaluate associations between radiotherapy protocols and outcomes; record the model class selected for the analysis run.
Primary radiotherapy protocol variable evaluated as the exposure in the analysis; describes the modeled protocol attribute rather than the estimated effect.
Primary outcome variable modeled in the analysis, such as survival or quality-of-life endpoint; record the endpoint targeted by the statistical model.
Approach used to adjust for covariates or confounding in the statistical model; measured as part of the analysis specification.
Whether the fitted model converged successfully and produced stable estimates during the analysis run.
Date when the protocol-outcome analysis run started; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.
Date when the protocol-outcome analysis run ended; use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD.

outcome_association_results.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed statistical result fields produced by the analysis: effect estimates, uncertainty intervals, p-values, comparison basis, and result-quality summaries. I excluded model configuration, software/runtime, and raw dataset properties because those belong to upstream Process or Derivative-supporting nodes, not the result object itself. I also avoided previously colliding generic identifiers such as software_name, software_version, repository_url, and other already-generated field names by using result-specific field IDs only.

md_schema.descr: Unique string identifier for this derived results object; format example: RES_001.
Type of statistical effect estimate reported for the protocol-outcome association, such as hazard ratio or odds ratio; measured from the fitted analysis model.
Numerical value of the primary protocol effect estimate produced by the analysis, such as a hazard ratio; report the point estimate from the fitted model.
Lower bound of the confidence interval for the primary effect estimate; report the bound produced by the statistical model.
Upper bound of the confidence interval for the primary effect estimate; report the bound produced by the statistical model.
Nominal confidence level used for the reported interval, typically 95 percent; record the level applied to all effect estimates in this result set.
P-value associated with the primary protocol effect estimate or hypothesis test; report the value returned by the statistical analysis.
Description of the reference or comparator group used to estimate the protocol effect, such as a specific radiotherapy protocol or regimen.
Number of outcome events contributing to the estimated association, such as deaths or QoL endpoint occurrences; count derived from the fitted analysis dataset.
Brief summary of model fit or diagnostic status for the derived association result, such as convergence or proportional-hazards adequacy.
